```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 4.5)
library(BayesianQDM)
```

## Designs built step by step

The native pipe `|>` of R (version 4.1.0 or later) passes the result of one
function to the first argument of the next. In BayesianQDM,
`qdm_endpoint()` starts a design specification for an endpoint, and each of
the other steps sets some arguments of the `design_*()` function of the
endpoint:

| Step | Arguments |
|---|---|
| `qdm_sample_size()` | `n_t`, `n_c` |
| `qdm_prior()` | `prior_t`, `prior_c` |
| `qdm_criterion()` | `criterion` |
| `qdm_external()` | `external_t`, `external_c` |
| `qdm_control()` | `hypothetical_c`, `fixed_c` |
| `qdm_tte()` | `milestone`, `effect`, `conduct`, `conduct_future` (time-to-event endpoint) |
| `qdm_computation()` | `method`, `nMC`, `enumerate` |

A specification can be printed at any step. Until the required arguments
are set, it lists those still needed:

```{r spec-start}
spec <- qdm_endpoint("binary") |>
  qdm_sample_size(n_t = 12, n_c = 12)
spec
```

Once the sample sizes, the prior distribution of the treatment group and the
decision criterion are set, it describes the design:

```{r spec-complete}
spec <- spec |>
  qdm_prior(prior_t = prior_beta(0.5, 0.5),
            prior_c = prior_beta(0.5, 0.5)) |>
  qdm_criterion(criterion_posterior(theta_tv = 0.2, theta_mav = 0.1,
                                    gamma_go = 0.5, gamma_nogo = 0.8))
spec
```

The steps only store their arguments. `qdm_build()` creates the design by
calling `design_binary()`, which checks the arguments, so the design is the
same as when `design_binary()` is called directly:

```{r build}
des <- design_binary(
  n_t = 12, n_c = 12,
  prior_t = prior_beta(0.5, 0.5), prior_c = prior_beta(0.5, 0.5),
  criterion = criterion_posterior(theta_tv = 0.2, theta_mav = 0.1,
                                  gamma_go = 0.5, gamma_nogo = 0.8)
)
identical(qdm_build(spec), des)
```

An invalid argument gives the error of `design_binary()` when the design is
built:

```{r error}
try(spec |> qdm_sample_size(n_t = 0, n_c = 12) |> qdm_build())
```

## From the design to the results

`qdm_decide()`, `qdm_oc()`, `qdm_calibrate()` and `qdm_boundary()` accept a
specification in place of a design and build it, and their results can be
passed on to `plot()`. The decision for 9 responders of 12 subjects in the
treatment group and 4 of 12 in the control group is

```{r decide}
spec |>
  qdm_decide(data_t = data_binary(12, 9), data_c = data_binary(12, 4))
```

The operating characteristics for true response rates of the treatment
group from 0.3 to 0.7, with a control response rate of 0.3, are

```{r oc}
scen <- data.frame(pi_t = seq(0.3, 0.7, by = 0.05), pi_c = 0.3)
spec |>
  qdm_oc(scen) |>
  plot()
```

The thresholds can be calibrated so that the probability of meeting the Go
criterion is at most 0.05 when the treatment has no effect, and that of
meeting the NoGo criterion is at most 0.2 when the effect is 0.3:

```{r calibrate}
cal <- spec |>
  qdm_calibrate(scenario_go = data.frame(pi_t = 0.3, pi_c = 0.3),
                scenario_nogo = data.frame(pi_t = 0.6, pi_c = 0.3),
                target_go = 0.05, target_nogo = 0.2)
cal
```

The calibrated thresholds are $\gamma_{go} =$ `r cal$gamma_go` and
$\gamma_{nogo} =$ `r cal$gamma_nogo`, and `cal$design` is the design with
these thresholds, which can start another pipe:

```{r calibrated}
cal$design |>
  qdm_decide(data_t = data_binary(12, 9), data_c = data_binary(12, 4))
```

The observed data that lead to each decision are

```{r boundary}
spec |>
  qdm_boundary() |>
  plot()
```

## Changing one step

A step given again replaces the arguments that it set before, so a
specification can be the start of several pipes that change one of its
parts. For example, the probabilities of a Go decision with no effect
($\pi_t = \pi_c = 0.2$) and with an effect of 0.3 ($\pi_t = 0.5$), for
sample sizes from 12 to 30 per group, are

```{r sample-size}
scen2 <- data.frame(pi_t = c(0.2, 0.5), pi_c = 0.2)
n <- c(12, 18, 24, 30)
go <- vapply(n, function(k) {
  oc <- spec |>
    qdm_sample_size(n_t = k, n_c = k) |>
    qdm_oc(scen2)
  oc$Go
}, numeric(2))
data.frame(n = n, no_effect = go[1, ], effect = go[2, ])
```

With `r n[4]` subjects per group, the probability of a Go decision is
`r format(go[2, 4], digits = 2)` with the effect of 0.3 and
`r format(go[1, 4], digits = 2)` with no effect, against
`r format(go[2, 1], digits = 2)` and `r format(go[1, 1], digits = 2)` with
`r n[1]` subjects per group.

External control data borrowed through a power prior:

```{r external}
spec |>
  qdm_external(external_c = borrow(data_binary(n = 40, y = 8), a0 = 0.5)) |>
  qdm_oc(scen2)
```

A criterion based on the posterior predictive probability of the effect
that will be observed in a future study with 50 subjects per group:

```{r predictive}
spec |>
  qdm_criterion(criterion_predictive(theta_null = 0.1, m_t = 50, m_c = 50,
                                     gamma_go = 0.8, gamma_nogo = 0.8)) |>
  qdm_decide(data_t = data_binary(12, 9), data_c = data_binary(12, 4))
```

A single-arm study of 20 subjects compared with a fixed control response
rate of 0.2, for which the control group has no prior distribution:

```{r fixed}
spec |>
  qdm_sample_size(n_t = 20, n_c = 0) |>
  qdm_prior(prior_t = prior_beta(0.5, 0.5)) |>
  qdm_control(fixed_c = 0.2) |>
  qdm_decide(data_t = data_binary(20, 9))
```

## Other endpoints

The steps are the same for every endpoint. `qdm_computation()` sets the
method of computation of the probabilities, for example the
moment-matching approximation for one continuous endpoint:

```{r continuous}
qdm_endpoint("continuous") |>
  qdm_sample_size(n_t = 15, n_c = 15) |>
  qdm_prior(prior_t = prior_vague(), prior_c = prior_vague()) |>
  qdm_criterion(criterion_posterior(theta_tv = 30, theta_mav = 15,
                                    gamma_go = 0.6, gamma_nogo = 0.7)) |>
  qdm_computation(method = "MM") |>
  qdm_oc(data.frame(mu_t = c(0, 20, 40), sd_t = 25, mu_c = 0, sd_c = 25),
         nsim = 2000, seed = 1)
```

`qdm_tte()` sets the arguments specific to a time-to-event endpoint, here
the hazard ratio as the effect measure, for which smaller effects are
favorable:

```{r tte}
qdm_endpoint("tte") |>
  qdm_sample_size(n_t = 30, n_c = 30) |>
  qdm_prior(prior_t = prior_gamma(0.1, 1), prior_c = prior_gamma(0.1, 1)) |>
  qdm_criterion(criterion_posterior(theta_tv = 0.67, theta_mav = 0.8,
                                    gamma_go = 0.5, gamma_nogo = 0.6,
                                    direction = "less")) |>
  qdm_tte(effect = "hazard_ratio") |>
  qdm_decide(data_t = data_tte(events = 12, exposure = 300),
             data_c = data_tte(events = 20, exposure = 260))
```

## Reports for a study protocol

`show_report()` can end a pipe. It writes the design, and the result passed
to it, as a draft of the corresponding sections of a study protocol: the
study design, the statistical model, the decision criteria with their
formulas, the computation of the probabilities and the result. The report
is an HTML file (`file_type = "html"`, the default), whose formulas are
displayed by MathJax, or a plain text file in Markdown format with the
formulas in LaTeX (`file_type = "text"`). It is written in a temporary file
unless `file` is given, and it is shown when R is used interactively
(`open`). Here the text report of the operating characteristics is printed:

```{r report}
spec |>
  qdm_oc(scen2) |>
  show_report(file_type = "text", open = TRUE)
```

The HTML report is written and opened in the same way:

```{r report-html, eval = FALSE}
spec |>
  qdm_oc(scen2) |>
  show_report(file = "decision_criteria.html")
```

The report gives the parts that depend on the design and the results. The
parts that depend on the study, such as the name of the endpoint and the
reasons for the target value and the minimum acceptable value, are to be
added in the protocol.
